To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

all of the drugs studied were mutagenic in Chinese hamster cell cultures, that the mutagenic responses were specific for different drugs and for different genetic loci, and that there was a very good correlation between the mutagenic activity of the drugs and their ability to induce sister chromatid exchanges.
13 antitumor drugs were tested for their mutagenicity in two different assay system in Chinese hamster cell lines, and that all drugs were mutagenic in both assay system.

the mutagenic responses to these drugs were specific for different chemical classes and for different genetic loci; the mutagenic activities of these drugs were correlated well with their sister chromatid exchange-inducing activities; the mutagenicity of the drugs differed by a factor of 100,000 in terms of the minimum concentrations required; and, finally, the mutagenicity was observed at concentrations which were much lower than those used in clinical practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of mutagenicity and carcinogenicity, with particular reference to the role of DNA repair and the induction of sister chromatid exchange as a possible mechanism of mutagenesis.
the development of an assay system for the detection of mutagenic agents in the human population.
the development of new methods to study the mutagenic effects of drugs and chemicals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these 13 antineoplastics, in the doses used in this study, are all mutagens, and that the hgprt locus is a useful genetic marker to detect mutagenic effects of antineoplastic agents in mammalian cells.
these drugs are mutagens in mammalian cells and that their mutagenic responses show specificity for different genetic loci.
these 13 anticancer drugs are mutagens in Chinese hamster cells and that their activity varies greatly in different assay systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all of these drugs are mutagenic at the hgprt gene, and that they also induce sister chromatid exchanges at a level that is directly related to their mutagenic activity at the hgprt genetic locus.
these antineoplastic agents are generally very potent mutagens in Chinese hamster cells and that their mutagenic responses can vary greatly from one locus to another.
all of the drugs which were studied are mutagenic at multiple genetic locuses and are also active in the induction of sister chromatid exchange.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a battery of different genetic loci and sister chromatid exchanges provides a sensitive and powerful approach to the detection of mutagenic and genotoxic responses of drugs and chemicals.

, in general, these anticancer drugs can be considered mutagenic, although their mutagenic responses are very specific in that they differ greatly from each other in their ability to produce mutations at different genetic loci.

, in addition to the sister chromatid exchanges assay which has been widely used in mutagenicity testing, the assay system which we have developed for measuring mutational changes at multiple genetic locus may also be useful in the evaluation of mutagenic activity of drugs.
